Q: In the future, will it be possible to use "VLA" in a struct in a C program? A:

To address the specific question.

I know that actually at compile type the struct size must be know. But in the future ?

We cannot predict the future, but I find it HIGHLY unlikely. Apart from the reasons in other answers, a very strong sign for this is that after they introduced VLA:s as a mandatory part in C99, they have afterwards made them optional already in the next version C11. This indicates that they found that allowing VLA:s was a mistake in the first place.

Q: Is it normal that std::unordered_map has different bucket_counts? A:

Yes, this is normal. Try to implement a bucket-based map from scratch, and you will see that there is some degree of arbitrariness in the way the set of keys is broken into buckets. This classification is based on the value of the hash code obtained from every key. Every time you get a new key and its hash code, you have to decide if you have to create a new bucket or add this key to an existing bucket closest by the hash code value. Note that at the moment of this decision, you don't know the total number of key-value pairs in the map during its lifetime. These decisions is a matter of optimization, so you have a trade-off between the complexity of this calculation and the optimization of the set of buckets. There is always a trade-off between redundancy (and, hence, memory usage) and performance.
(Note that two extremes, either exactly 1 bucket or the number of buckets equal to the number of keys would defeat the purpose of the algorithm, leading to the time complexity of O(N), that is, always the worst-case scenario possible for the bucket system. The optimal decision will be somewhere in between.)

I am not sure if you put any difference in your sample compared to the sample on this page, but the number of buckets can be implementation-dependent. Note the word possible in possible output.

Q: Cassandra creates multiple connections and not release A:

If Cassandra creates multiple connections and does not release them, it usually means:

  • Sessions are not being closed properly

  • Connection pooling is misconfigured

  • Objects are created repeatedly (inside loops / per request)

  • Application is not reusing the cluster/session

Why Cassandra Creates Multiple Connections?

If you're using DataStax Java Driver, every time you create:

CqlSession session = CqlSession.builder().build();

Creating session inside a method:

public void insertData() {
    CqlSession session = CqlSession.builder().build();
    session.execute("INSERT INTO users ...");
}
